message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic identity** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Symbol | H |
| | Standard atomic weight | 1.00794 u (average of isotopes) |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | State at STP | Colorless, odorless, tasteless gas |
| | Density at STP | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ (≈1/11 of air) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (121 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14 K) |
| | Refractive index | 1.00028 (air) |
| | Molar volume (ideal gas) | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| **Physical constants** | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Electron affinity | 72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 432 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Heat capacity (gas, 25 °C) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Thermal conductivity | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 300 K) |
| | Specific heat (liquid, 20 °C) | 14.3 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| **Chemical behavior** | Diatomic molecule (H₂) | Stable under normal conditions |
| | Highly reactive | Forms covalent bonds with many elements |
| | Acidic in water | Forms H₃O⁺ (pKa ≈ –1.7) |
| | Forms hydrides | e.g., NaH, CaH₂, LiAlH₄ |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic) |
| | Redox potential | H⁺/H₂ couple E° = 0 V (vs SHE) |
| | Solubility in water | 0.0006 M at 25 °C |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Very soluble in liquid ammonia, ethanol, etc. |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (¹H) | Stable, most common (99.98 %) |
| | Deuterium (²H) | Stable, 1 % natural abundance |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive, half‑life 12.32 y, used in fusion research |
| | Nuclear spin | ¹H: ½, ²H: 1, ³H: ½ |
| **Applications** | Fuel & energy | Hydrogen fuel cells, rocket propellant (LH₂/LOX) |
| | Chemical industry | Ammonia synthesis (Haber process), methanol, hydrogenation reactions |
| | Metallurgy | Reducing agent for iron ore, steelmaking |
| | Electronics & materials | Used in semiconductor processing, plasma etching |
| | Medical & scientific | Tracer studies, MRI contrast agents (deuterated compounds) |
| | Environmental | Potential clean‑energy vector, water splitting for renewable H₂ |
| **Safety & handling** | Flammability range | 4 %–75 % in air |
| | Explosion limits | Lower limit 4 %, upper limit 75 % (by volume) |
| | Toxicity | Non‑toxic; inhalation can cause hypoxia due to displacement of oxygen |
| | Storage | Requires high‑pressure cylinders (up to 700 bar) or cryogenic tanks |

---

### Quick Takeaways

* Hydrogen is the lightest element, existing naturally as a diatomic gas (H₂) at room temperature.
* It has a very low boiling/melting point, making it a gas under most Earth conditions.
* Its chemical reactivity is high; it readily forms covalent bonds and is a key player in acid–base chemistry.
* Isotopic variants (protium, deuterium, tritium) give hydrogen unique nuclear and spectroscopic properties.
* Hydrogen’s role in energy technology (fuel cells, rockets) and industrial processes (ammonia, methanol) makes it central to modern chemistry and future clean‑energy strategies.
